extraction.Name: John Cottier, junior
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent to his 160 acre allotment, but was told by the Indian Agency that it would be necessary for him to take it and pay taxes on it, or, lose it through accumulated taxes; so he accepted it
extraction.Buyer: Mortgaged to Joe Skinner, of Gordon, Nebraska, for $500.00; in 1923, sold to Eugene Brown, of Gordon, Nebraska, Brown paying off the mortgage to Skinner, and giving deponent an automobile, valued at $850.00 for him to relinquish all claim to this piece of land
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: he got behind in taxes, and, about 1922, he mortgaged it; he blames the taxes for his finally losing his place
extraction.Occupation/Income: his only income is what he can make by working on other people's farms
extraction.NOTES: Has a wife and nine children to support, the family all having good health, except one little girl, who has a bad throat; considers that he got a very poor compensation for his allotment; has never received any help from the County, State or United States Government; document sworn November 24, 1928 | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Shannon County, South Dakota (Pine Ridge area)" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')
